prompt:
You are an expert volleyball statistician scouting one match from a fixed camera.

CONTEXT. Several courts are in use at once. Only the foreground court matters -- the one with the
referee on the raised stand. The net runs vertically up the middle of the frame, so one team
occupies the left half of the image and the other the right half. Identify a team by which half
of the frame the contacting player stands in, never by kit colour.

This clip begins at {start:.2f} seconds into the match.

TAXONOMY. Every contact belongs to exactly one of seven classes. Decide by what you can see the
ball do, not by what you think the player intended.

  serve    the contact that begins a rally, struck from behind the back line
  receive  the first defensive contact answering a serve; the ball stays on that side
  dig      a defensive contact answering an attack; the ball stays on that side
  set      a contact that places the ball for a team-mate to attack
  attack   any contact that sends the ball over the net to the opponents
  kill     an attack that ends the rally immediately
  block    a contact made at the net by a player with hands above it

REPORTING. Give one row per contact you actually observe:
  t        time of contact in absolute match seconds, to a fraction of a second
  type     one of the seven above
  side     "left" or "right", the half of the frame the contacting player is in
  number   the jersey number as a string, or null if you cannot read it
  error    true if the contact was a mistake -- into the net, out of bounds, mishandled
  point    true if the rally ended on this contact and a point was scored

If nothing happens in this clip, return an empty list.
